correctness.rationale: The Fano incidence equations for positive-spin subsets give B+Q=2k(4−k)+8N₃−7, Q=(−1)^{3−|S∩ℓ*|}, and M=2k−7. An independent census using kernels of the seven nonzero linear forms on F₂³ and binary spin parity reproduced all 16 signatures, all 128 configurations and every multiplicity. At u>0 a sector with fixed (B,Q) contributes only maximal M. Of the six resulting candidates, (0,−1,3) is strictly above A for u<3 and strictly above C₋ for u>1, which exhaust u>0. The retained lines have multiplicities 7,9,4,3,1. For λ<1, C₊ beats C₋, the B–C₊ and C₊–D crossings are 1 and 3, and comparison of A with B and C₊ gives the cuts λ=−2 and −1 and the tabulated fields. For λ>1, C₋ beats C₊, B cannot beat both A and C₋, and the remaining crossings are 2 and 2+λ. At λ=1 the C branches coincide, so all minimizing multiplicities must be added; the named coexistence counts follow. At u=0 the minima of the Q=−1 and Q=+1 sectors are −6−λ and −2+λ with counts 8 and 24, so the tie has count 32 and positive marked product costs at least two other positive line products. Opposite-spin pairing of the fixed-(B,Q) counts yields the three cosh coefficients 16,64,48.
residual_risks: The phase classification is for strictly positive field; the zero-field degeneracies have a separate rule. No thermodynamic-limit or quantum claim follows.

value.rationale: The symmetric seven-site design is a natural finite model for the effect of changing the sign of one triple. Full coverage of the two parameters gives a sharp cost of two frustrated ordinary lines, marked-coupling thresholds, magnetization jumps, and all coexistence multiplicities. The joint census is an exact benchmark for parity-model partition calculations, not just a grid of sample energies.
residual_risks: Interpretation is finite-size and restricted to a single changed coupling; no many-defect or thermodynamic behavior is established.
